findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' (Tennyson) and 'Bayonet Charge' (Ted Hughes) as poems of 'The Conflict poetry collection in the OCR anthology'.
findings.truth: Neither poem is in the OCR Conflict cluster. 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' is in the AQA Power and Conflict and Edexcel Conflict clusters; 'Bayonet Charge' is AQA Power and Conflict. The OCR Conflict cluster is 15 poems: A Poison Tree (Blake), Envy (Mary Lamb), Boat Stealing from the 1799 Prelude (Wordsworth), The Destruction of Sennacherib (Byron), There's a Certain Slant of Light (Dickinson), The Man He Killed (Hardy), Anthem for Doomed Youth (Owen), Vergissmeinnicht (Keith Douglas), What Were They Like? (Levertov), Lament (Gillian Clarke), Punishment (Heaney), Flag (Agard), Phrase Book (Jo Shapcott), Honour Killing (Imtiaz Dharker), Partition (Sujata Bhatt). A student revising this lesson would learn two poems that cannot be named on their paper. Rebuild the lesson on the real soldier-experience poems: The Man He Killed, Anthem for Doomed Youth, Vergissmeinnicht.

findings.truth: There is no 'typically'. findings.claim: 'How should you split time on the 40-mark comparison?' with the keyed answer '5 plan, 35-40 write, 5 check' (and the matching item '35-40 minutes' = writing).
findings.truth: There is no 40-mark comparison. The poetry section is 40 marks in TWO parts of 20. With 2 hours for 80 marks the poetry section gets about 60 minutes, so each 20-mark part gets about 30 minutes: roughly 5 minutes planning, 22 writing, 3 checking. The keyed answer sends a student 15-20 minutes over on one part.

findings.claim: Across all eight lessons, 24 questions are labelled '40 marks - Poetry Comparison' with mark schemes reading 'AO1 (up to 15 marks) / AO2 (up to 15 marks) / AO3 (up to 10 marks)', and 24 are labelled '20 marks - Extract Comparison' with ladders that top out at 10 marks ('Top band (9-10) ... Lower band (1-2)').
findings.truth: Three separate errors. (1) No poetry question on this paper is worth 40 marks; both parts are 20. (2) The AO split 15/15/10 is invented - the spec publishes no per-AO mark split for the poetry question, and the component-level weightings are AO1 20%, AO2 22.5%, AO3 5%, AO4 2.5%, with AO4 in the Shakespeare section only. (3) Nothing in the poetry section is extract-based, and a 10-mark ladder cannot label a 20-mark question; 'Lower band' is also off the house ladder and 'Mid band' is missing. I have deliberately NOT rescaled these ladders: all 48 questions either name an off-cluster poem or are study-skills prompts rather than exam tasks, so all 48 need rewriting with the poems, and rescaling now would mask that. On rebuild use 20-mark house bands: Top (17-20), Upper-mid (13-16), Mid (9-12), Lower-mid (5-8), Low (1-4).

findings.claim: 'A half-formed ghost begins to twist before his eyes, / a stranger's features / faintly start to materialise.'
findings.truth: Fabricated. Duffy's lines are 'A stranger's features / faintly start to twist before his eyes, / a half-formed ghost.' The lesson reverses the order and invents 'begins to' and 'materialise'.

findings.claim: 'The final stanza's image of the city "branded" on their hands'.
findings.truth: Fabricated wording and wrong placement. Rumens writes 'but I am branded by an impression of sunlight', and it is the last line of the FIRST stanza. There is no 'branded on the hands' anywhere in the poem.

findings.claim: 'In every cry of every Man, / In every Infant's cry of fear, / I hear / ... the mind-forg'd manacles I hear.'
findings.truth: Mangled. Blake's stanza is 'In every cry of every Man, / In every Infant's cry of fear, / In every voice, in every ban, / The mind-forg'd manacles I hear.' The lesson invents a line 'I hear /' and drops 'In every voice, in every ban'.
findings.evidence: William Blake, 'London', Songs of Experience (1794), public domain - stanza 2.

findings.claim: Q: 'Which simile depicts soldiers as engulfed by fire?' A: "'Rolled like a flame.'"
findings.truth: In 'Bayonet Charge' the simile describes the yellow hare - 'a yellow hare that rolled like a flame' - not soldiers. Lesson 1 of this unit states the hare correctly, so the flashcard contradicts the lesson.
findings.evidence: Ted Hughes, 'Bayonet Charge', The Hawk in the Rain (1957), stanza 2; lesson 1 content_html of this unit.

findings.claim: '600 British soldiers charged directly into Russian artillery. Around 110 were killed and 160 wounded.'
findings.truth: About 670 men charged; roughly 110-118 were killed and 127-134 wounded. 'Six hundred' is Tennyson's poetic figure, not the muster roll. The wounded figure is about 30 too high.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_of_the_Light_Brigade - about 670 charged, 113-118 killed, 127-134 wounded, about 60 taken prisoner.

summary: Unit-fatal: 7 of the 8 poems taught are not in the OCR Conflict cluster - they are AQA Power and Conflict and Edexcel Conflict poems. Only 'A Poison Tree' belongs. The exam model taught (a 40-mark comparison of two anthology poems, split AO1 15 / AO2 15 / AO3 10, labelled 'Extract Comparison') does not exist: the real task is one compulsory question in two 20-mark parts - (a) the named anthology poem against an unseen poem printed on the paper, (b) a related question on a different anthology poem of the student's own choice. Recommend rebuilding all eight lessons against the 15 real poems; the edits attached fix the fabricated quotations and the exam-structure claims so the live rows are less misleading in the meantime.
